rows.title: Vault deployment
rows.proves: The enforcement contract exists on-chain with the owner as Ownable2Step owner. Source verification status is recorded in the runbook.

rows.title: Owner sets agent, asset mandates, allowlists
rows.fn: setAgent, setAssetMandate, setAssetMandate, setAllowedTarget, setAllowedTarget, setAllowedSelector
rows.proves: The mandate (expiry, per-asset caps, allowlisted targets and selectors) is on-chain state set only by the owner.

rows.title: ERC-8004 registration of both agents and setAgentWallet to the vault
rows.fn: register(agentURI) x2, setAgentWallet(agentId, vault, deadline, ownerSig)
rows.outcome: our agent #10052, oracle agent #10053 in registry 0x8004A818BFB912233c491871b3d84c89A494BD9e; vault bound as agent wallet
rows.proves: Both agents carry a portable on-chain identity. The vault is the registered wallet of our agent, bound with the owner's ERC-1271 signature; the agent key alone cannot make that binding.

rows.title: Tier 1 autonomous ETH transfer to an allowlisted contact
rows.proves: Inside the mandate the agent transacts alone: active agent, allowlisted target, within per-tx and window caps, nonce consumed.

rows.title: Tier 1 WETH wrap through an allowlisted contract call
rows.proves: Contract calls are restricted to allowlisted (target, selector) pairs and the calldata hash is bound into the signed intent.

rows.title: Petty cash top-up from the vault to the agent EOA
rows.proves: The imprest float: a small, capped USDC balance the agent can spend on x402 invoices, replenished only from the vault and only to itself.

rows.title: x402 USDC payment to the oracle agent from petty cash
rows.proves: An agent paying another agent per request: the EIP-3009 authorization is signed by the agent's petty cash account and settled on-chain by the facilitator. The vault is never involved in the payment itself.

rows.title: Over-cap attempt by the agent key, directly against the vault
rows.proves: The per-transaction cap is enforced by the chain, not by the agent software. A compromised agent key cannot exceed it.

rows.title: Transfer to a non-allowlisted target
rows.proves: Counterparties outside the allowlist need an owner co-signature; without one the chain reverts.

rows.title: Tier 2 co-signed transfer: owner EIP-712 approval verified on-chain
rows.proves: Above the autonomous caps or outside the allowlist, the contract itself checks the owner's signature over this exact intent hash and deadline.

rows.title: Replay of the same owner approval on a new intent
rows.proves: An approval is bound to one intent hash; the nonce makes every intent hash unique, so a captured approval cannot be reused.

rows.title: Window cap exhaustion through repeated sub-cap transfers
rows.proves: The daily window is a blast-radius bound: many small transfers cannot add up to more than the owner allowed.

rows.title: Kill switch: revokeAgent then any agent call reverts; pause likewise
rows.fn: revokeAgent, execute, setAgent, pause, execute, unpause
rows.outcome: after revoke: AgentNotActive(); after pause: EnforcedPause()
rows.proves: One owner transaction ends the agent's authority. In-flight and future agent transactions revert on-chain.

rows.title: EIP-7702 delegation and one execution through MandateAccount7702
Tier 3: unlimited token approval, even with an owner approval
rows.proves: Some actions have no code path at all. No signature lifts a Tier 3 restriction.
